extracted.intended_audience: general readers and researchers interested in Canadian history, plagiarism/copyright law, and the H. G. Wells controversy
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article summarizing the life, work, and legal struggles of Florence Deeks, with emphasis on her plagiarism claim against H. G. Wells and the judicial findings at multiple court levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility of literary criticism as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence presented on the basis of literary criticism is not admissible in a court of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lord Atkin (for the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council) stated this principle when dismissing Deeks's appeal; this implies that expert stylistic/textual analyses may be excluded from legal consideration when offered as proof of copying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof requirement for copying in plagiarism/copyright cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The court found no proof of copying where it was sworn the manuscript remained in Toronto and Wells did not even know it existed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plaintiffs must show that the defendant had access to (or opportunity to see) the plaintiff's manuscript and that copying occurred; mere thematic or textual similarities without evidence of access are generally insufficient for a successful claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Similarity may reflect common sources or similar nature rather than copying
rubrics_metrics.description: The court decided the similarities were due to the fact that the books had similar nature and both writers had access to the same sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing alleged plagiarism, consider whether overlapping content can be explained by shared source material or genre conventions rather than direct copying; identical wording is rare and identical mistakes, while notable, are not definitive proof on their own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate legal characterization of the claim (breach of confidence vs copyright)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although Deeks claimed breach of copyright, in substance she was claiming breach of confidence in the use of her manuscript without consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful selection and framing of the legal cause of action is important; plaintiffs should align the substantive facts and desired remedies with the correct legal theory (e.g., breach of confidence vs copyright infringement) to avoid procedural or substantive mismatches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual and non-legal factors affecting litigation outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The case may have been lost in part due to bias against Deeks as a woman and her lack of influential connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical and social context (including potential gender bias and differences in resources or connections) can influence judicial processes and outcomes; assessments of past cases should account for these factors in addition to strictly legal standards.
